static_traits.name: Han Na
static_traits.social_status: Has a group of cycling-loving friends, but interactions with them are affected by feelings of self-inadequacy
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no history of psychological counseling or treatment in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression and good organization, able to be aware of and describe automatic thoughts, slightly tense emotionally but positive in attitude and high in cooperation

basic_info.main_problem: After getting a flat tire during a ride and being unable to fix it alone, began seeing oneself as a 'bad rider', producing feelings of incompetence and failure, avoiding cycling and repeatedly doubting oneself.
basic_info.core_demands: Because a flat tire incident and the negative automatic thoughts it triggered affected overall mood and confidence, seeking counseling to improve this state.
growth_experiences: A few weeks ago a flat tire during a ride left Han Na frustrated and helpless for being unable to fix it on the spot. Since the event, the thought 'I am a bad rider' has recurred; she began avoiding cycling, tried bike repairs and short rides, but the negative feelings persist. This has affected her cycling-related performance in athletic work, strained relationships with cycling-loving friends, and impacted daily exercise and physical condition.

core_beliefs: I am not competent enough / I am incompetent (especially in cycling)
One failure proves I am no good overall

special_situations.event: Seeing a bicycle or thinking about going cycling
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I get another flat tire and cannot fix it on the spot, it will expose my incompetence for others to see
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids going out cycling, or only tries shorter, more conservative routes to reduce risk
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will get another flat tire and cannot fix it; everyone will know I am no good

special_situations.event: When friends talk about cycling or invite one to ride together
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I perform poorly, I will be judged as unqualified and not accepted
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing participation or not discussing true feelings with friends, to avoid being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am an incompetent rider

special_situations.event: Recalling the last flat tire experience
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One failure can prove my overall incompetence
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Labeling oneself a 'terrible rider', using it to explain and avoid trying again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I messed it up that time, which proves I am just no good

special_situations.event: Preparing to plan a new ride or training session
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I must not make a single mistake, otherwise it is total failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly checks and seeks others' company, postponing longer or more challenging rides
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I make even a small mistake again, it proves I am simply not suited for cycling

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be seen as a competent athlete worthy of recognition, gaining peers' acceptance and respect
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being humiliated, negated or excluded for exposing incompetence
defense_goal: Protecting self-esteem by avoiding cycling and reducing self-exposure
Not talking about feelings to avoid criticism or judgment

object_relations.self_representation: An incompetent failure who may err at any time
object_relations.object_representation: Critical others/peers who could judge one's ability at any time

object_relations.self_representation: A rider craving support and needing to be understood
object_relations.object_representation: Friends who may offer support and help
object_relations.linking_affect: Hope, ease (in the imagination of being supported)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When friends talk about cycling or invite one to ride together
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: They will look down on me, treating me as an unqualified rider (transference projection)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Hesitant tone, vague wording, avoiding clear commitments; reducing exposure by deflecting topics or postponing.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When facing longer distances or more challenging cycling/training arrangements
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: One mistake means total failure and being negated by others
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Politely declines by emphasizing outside reasons such as time arrangements or physical state, in a peaceful tone but tending toward avoidance, avoiding touching on the emotional topic of one's own ability.

manifestations: Avoiding cycling reducing interaction with cycling friends, relationship tension
Unwilling to express true anxiety and inadequacy to friends, creating psychological distance
outcomes: Social estrangement and underutilized support systems
Avoidance behavior maintains the problem cycle

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Criticizes oneself with 'I am a bad rider', reduces willingness to contact and try with others
Over-worries about possible mistakes when planning a ride, reduces or postpones action

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Assuming friends will see oneself as unqualified, thus reducing participation and sharing
In social situations, over-interprets others' potential evaluations

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Treating 'no mistakes allowed while cycling' as a hard standard, engaging in self-denial at any slip
Viewing an event such as one flat tire as a verdict on overall ability

exception_events.target_problem: When seeing a bicycle or thinking of cycling, Han Na usually experiences strong anxiety and self-denial, coping through avoidance or only very short rides, affecting training and work.
exception_events.unique_outcome: For a period after the event, she watched tutorials on changing tires on her own and carried out actual practice, thereby becoming clearer about the steps for handling a flat tire and feeling 'knowing better what to do'.
exception_events.reason: Different approach: proactive learning and hands-on practice; different understanding: turning uncontrollable events (flat tires) into masterable skill steps, increasing sense of control.

positive_force: Years of cycling experience and athletic background, providing a foundation for rebuilding confidence
Has friends who love cycling as a potential support resource
Able to proactively learn and practice (watches tutorials and hands-on practices changing a tire)
Positive attitude, willing to try short rides and ride with friends for gradual exposure
negative_force: Catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking reinforcing the sense of failure
Mind-reading-style prediction of others' evaluations, over-reliance on external approval
Avoidance behaviors maintaining anxiety and self-doubt
Labeling oneself (incompetent), ignoring positive evidence from years of cycling
Lacking emotional communication with friends, so the support system has not yet been effectively used

antecedent: Friends talking about or inviting a bike ride
target_behavior.core_reason: The flat-tire experience triggering doubts about ability and shameful anticipation, worrying that failing again in front of others will expose 'incompetence'.
target_behavior.function: Escaping anxiety and potential shame/negative evaluation, gaining safety in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Professional training and performance affected, less daily exercise, overall mood and decreased confidence

target_behavior.behavior: Negative automatic thoughts and self-labels (such as 'I am a terrible rider')
antecedent: Planning or preparing for a new bike ride
target_behavior.core_reason: Overgeneralizing one failure as overall incompetence, using external evaluation as the reference for self-worth.
target_behavior.function: Providing inner justification for avoidance, trying to reduce the pressure of trying again through self-denial
target_behavior.consequence: Inferiority and anxiety maintained, behavior more avoidant, missing positive corrective experiences

target_behavior.behavior: Reducing interaction and sharing with cycling friends (social withdrawal)
antecedent: Being invited to join a cycling event
target_behavior.core_reason: Mind-reading assumption that others will negate oneself, fearing humiliation or exclusion after exposing weaknesses.
target_behavior.function: Avoiding possible negative evaluations and embarrassment
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced social support, increased sense of isolation, negative self-schemas reinforced
